findings.title: High-frequency statistical arbitrage repos: noterminusgit/statarb (production-grade, 20+ alpha strategies, PCA/Barra), bradleyboyuyang/Statistical-Arbitrage, gregzanotti/dlsa-public
findings.note: None of these three appear anywhere in wiki/ or dream_cycle/ (confirmed via grep). statarb (noterminusgit) is the most feature-complete -- PCA decomposition + Barra risk models + realistic TC modeling across ~1,400 US equities -- structurally similar to our H198/H241 momentum universe scale, but star count could not be confirmed this session (WebSearch did not surface it) and its true novelty vs. our existing vectorbt-based pipeline (H510-514 OB-filter family, H198 grid sweeps) is unclear without a deeper read. Not staged tonight -- flagging as a candidate for a future session to verify star count/activity via GitHub API and assess whether its Barra-style risk decomposition offers anything our current per-hypothesis Sharpe/MaxDD gate doesn't, rather than writing a wiki entry on an unverified repo.

summary.note: Second consecutive dry night on all 5 angles, consistent with 2026-08-24's own note that broad topic-search saturation had been reached. Every high-relevance-looking hit across 4 of 5 angles was checked via grep against wiki/ and dream_cycle/ and confirmed already ingested (in several cases, e.g. ai-hedge-fund, with a full dedicated section already written by a prior session). The GitHub angle surfaced one genuinely-not-yet-logged item (noterminusgit/statarb) but it was deliberately NOT staged: risk_level would require either a 'medium' wiki_update (acceptable) but the repo's actual novelty vs. our stack is unverified -- writing it up without confirming star count/license/activity would violate this project's verification discipline (the same GitHub-API-first practice used for Homerun in tonight's Phase 1 wiki page). Flagged in this finding's note for a future session to verify properly before writing. Reinforces 2026-08-24's suggestion: future scans should use more targeted queries (arXiv category+date listing pages, GitHub topic pages sorted by recent push) rather than broad topic search, which is now surfacing mostly repeat hits across this maturing wiki.
